subject: ECON
course_description: This course is designed to provide students the opportunity to explore issues in economic development viewed from the perspective of sub-Saharan Africa from the impact of slavery and colonialism to the modern era of globalization.
course_notes: (Same as AFS 366W 1) Updated Course Description: This course covers theories and concepts for addressing real-world issues, as well as their applications to Africa's development discourse and policy options. It explores Africa's contemporary economic development issues from competing perspectives. Topics covered include the economic implications of demographic asymmetries, "variable geometries" in geopolitics, and postmodernism (i.e., the Fourth Industrial Revolution). Emphasis is on understanding public choice and the role of institutions in mediating transactions in both economic and political markets. The influence of domestic and international actors on the domestic policies of African countries is highlighted, providing a practical understanding of how these issues play out in the 21st Century.
